newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian opposition suspends protest for 3 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition suspends protest for 3 weeks.

text.p: Serbia's opposition said on Saturday they would suspend their marathon street protests for three weeks to give the government time to liberalise the state-run media.

Zoran Djindjic, co-leader of the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition, told demonstrators on the 88th day of street protests: "Let us give them a chance to show an intention to free the media and, if they fail to do that by March 9, then what else can we do but go out into the streets again."

Djindjic told around 10,000 demonstrators in central Belgrade -- a fraction of the 500,000 who took to the streets at the height of the protests -- that they had achieved one of their main aims, the recognition of opposition gains in local elections, but that they still had two key goals.

"Our three objectives were to get back our election victory, and achieve the deblocking of the media and fair conditions ahead of the next elections. We have achieved the first, but not the other two."
"We shall give them three weeks, until March 9 -- let us see what will happen by March 9," Djindjic said.
"After the media are freed, we shall talk about fair conditions for the elections, and a new election financing law," he added.
